title: Boats and Streams
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Boats and Streams. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Current changes ground speed

Let b be a boat's speed in still water and s the current speed. Downstream motion is aided by the current, so its speed is b+s. Upstream motion is opposed, so its speed is b-s, provided b>s. These formulas assume the current and boat speed stay constant.

If downstream and upstream speeds are known, add them and halve to find b; subtract and halve to find s. Use distance divided by the appropriate ground speed to find travel time. Do not add the current speed in both directions.

Worked example: A boat goes downstream at 18 km/h and upstream at 12 km/h. Still-water speed is (\(18+12\))/2=15 km/h; current speed is (\(18-12\))/2=3 km/h.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Label each speed as upstream, downstream, still-water or current.
  • Use the sum for still-water speed and the difference for current speed.
  • Check that upstream speed is positive and smaller than downstream speed.
  • Use consistent distance units in round-trip problems.
  • For equal distances, do not take the arithmetic mean of unequal speeds.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Downstream speed = b+s. Upstream speed = b-s.
  • Still-water speed = (\(downstream + upstream\))/2.
  • Current speed = (downstream - upstream)/2.
  • Time = distance / ground speed.
  • For equal distances at speeds D and U, average speed = 2DU/(\(D+U\)).

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A boat travels downstream at 18 km/h and upstream at 12 km/h. What is the stream speed?

    1. (\(2\text{ km/h}\))
    2. (\(3\text{ km/h}\))
    3. (\(5\text{ km/h}\))
    4. (\(6\text{ km/h}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3\text{ km/h}\))

    Stream speed (\(=(18-12)/2=3\text{ km/h}\)).

  2. Core:

    A boat's still-water speed is 10 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. How long does it take to travel 32 km upstream?

    1. (\(3\text{ h}\))
    2. (\(4\text{ h}\))
    3. (\(5\text{ h}\))
    4. (\(6\text{ h}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(4\text{ h}\))

    Upstream speed (\(=10-2=8\text{ km/h}\)). Time (\(=32/8=4\)) hours.

  3. Foundation:

    A boat's downstream speed is 20 km/h and upstream speed is 12 km/h. Find the current speed.

    1. (\(2 km/h\))
    2. (\(4 km/h\))
    3. (\(6 km/h\))
    4. (\(8 km/h\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(4 km/h\))

    Current speed is half the difference: (\((20-12)/2=4\)) km/h.

  4. Standard:

    A boat's still-water speed is 16 km/h and the current is 4 km/h. How long does a 48 km upstream trip take?

    1. (\(3 h\))
    2. (\(4 h\))
    3. (\(5 h\))
    4. (\(6 h\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(4 h\))

    Upstream speed is (\(16-4=12\)) km/h. Time is (\(48/12=4\)) hours.

  5. Challenge:

    A boat covers equal distances upstream at 12 km/h and downstream at 20 km/h. What is its average speed for the round trip?

    1. (\(14 km/h\))
    2. (\(15 km/h\))
    3. (\(16 km/h\))
    4. (\(16.5 km/h\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(15 km/h\))

    For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: (\(2 × 12 × 20/(12+20)=15\)) km/h.
